title: Violin, piano and trumpet lessons with Paulin Fabian
summary: He played violin well enough to double, studied trumpet with a former Republican Guard Band musician, and earned $8 at his first engagement at 12.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: I never heard of him. My brother was a trombonist. I played the violin fairly well, enough to double. And I attempted piano, just for the harmony, you know. But I had the finest trumpet teacher in the world. He was a member of the Republican Guard Band of France. He came here with the French Opera Company. And my father believed in good instruction. And I got it.

Pardon? P-A-U-L-I-N. F-A-B-I-A-N. Fabian. Fabian. I made my first professional engagement when I was 12, standing on the Coca-Cola box, playing at a mass meeting, political meeting. I got eight dollars. I was a rich man that night.
